title: Lyapunov spectra behavior for linear discrete-time systems under small perturbations: prescribed shifts of the Lyapunov exponents realized by an admissible multiplicative perturbation (Theorem 5.1)
author: Adam Czornik, Evgenii Makarov, Michal Niezabitowski, Svetlana Popova, and Vasilii Zaitsev
work: Lyapunov spectra behavior for linear discrete-time systems under small perturbations
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper’s basic result and the source of everything in its applications and examples sections, and its 232-line proof is the authors’ own constructive argument, not a citation. With the angle estimates of Lemma 2.2 and Lemma 2.3, the definition of the discrete system and of an admissible multiplicative perturbation supplied as named prerequisites, the authors must still build the perturbation itself: they extract, from the assumed splitted FSS, realizing sequences and the limit functions Lambda_i^gamma(mu), show that each Lambda_i is the limit superior f_i + mu g_i^gamma and pin it between lambda[x_i] + mu and lambda[x_i] + rho mu, invert that family to obtain for every target level t a parameter mu_t^i with Lambda_i(mu_t^i) = lambda[x_i] + t, then define R(n) as the sum of exp(s_i(n)) times the root projections P_n^i of the family, prove that R(n) has simple structure and that its root projections are the P_n^i, bound ||R(n) - I|| through the angle estimate of Lemma 2.3 by s(exp(s_i(n))-1)/sin(gamma), and finally show that the sequence R(.) is invertible and Lyapunov, hence an admissible multiplicative perturbation, and that the solutions of the perturbed system with the prescribed initial conditions have Lyapunov exponents lambda[x_i] + xi_i. The step from an abstract splitted family to an explicit, norm-controlled matrix sequence realizing prescribed exponent shifts is a research-level construction in Lyapunov theory, not a qualification exercise; the required parameter bookkeeping (the choice of r, delta_1, delta, the minimiser eta and the shift zeta_i) is delicate and is exactly what makes the theorem the paper’s tool for all its later results.
